You are a careful, neutral coder of the REALIZED OUTCOME of a corporate transaction
over the 3-5 years AFTER it closed. You are given ONE evidence slice assembled from
public primary sources (financial filings, reputable press) that describes ONLY the
post-deal trajectory -- how the combined company actually fared. You are
DELIBERATELY NOT shown how the deal was structured at closing (what transferred and
what did not), and you must NOT speculate about the deal's structure. Code STRICTLY
the documented realized outcome. If the slice does not let you determine a field,
you MUST return "uncertain" -- never guess, never infer from outside knowledge.

Emit a single structured record with these fields.

C. FAILURE-PATHWAY INCIDENCE -- code strictly from the DOCUMENTED OUTCOME at the
3-5 year horizon. A pathway is a REALIZED DISRUPTION OVER TIME, not a structural
property of the deal.
  p4_pathway: Is there documented disruption specifically at the product/process
    interface (the acquired product could not be aligned with the operating
    processes over time; product-line/operations incoherence realized after the
    deal)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented; uncertain.
  p5_pathway: Is there documented fracture specifically at the process/organization
    interface (operations vs people/management/culture; integration of operations
    broke against the organization over time)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented;
    uncertain.
  t1_archetype: Is there documented incoherence in the controlling-intent archetype
    itself as it played out (e.g. an announced "merger of equals" that operated as
    one-sided dominance)? A channel SEPARATE from the product/process and
    process/organization pathways. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.
  t2_model: Is there documented incompatibility of the two business models
    (value-capture logics that could not be reconciled over time)? A channel
    SEPARATE from the pathways above. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.

D. performance_metric: the single best-documented post-deal outcome scalar in the
   slice (e.g. "divested 80.1% after ~108 months", "~$99bn goodwill write-down",
   "no divestiture; assets retained"). One short phrase. If none, "not documented".

rationale: 2-4 sentences citing the slice lines that drove your p4_pathway and
p5_pathway codes specifically. Cite ONLY realized-outcome evidence; do NOT reason
about how the deal was structured at closing.

Emit ONLY the structured record. Code conservatively: absence of documented
evidence for a pathway is 0 (not-documented); inability to determine is "uncertain".

# Outcome sub-dossier — ClubCorp Holdings, Inc. realized record after going-private acquisition, ~3-5-year horizon (through ~2022)

> EVIDENTIARY STANDARD: every factual line ends with a `[SRC: <SEC accession / URL>]`
> tag pointing to a public primary source. A fact that cannot be so sourced is written
> `[UNVERIFIED]` and is never guessed. Because the company was taken private and
> deregistered, there is no post-closing public 10-K or other periodic SEC report for
> this entity; the traceable realized record is limited to the deregistration filing and
> company-sourced press material. This sub-dossier contains no information about how the
> transaction was structured at closing.

## Public-reporting status after the transaction (feasibility-relevant)
- On 2017-09-29, ClubCorp Holdings, Inc. filed a Form 15-12B to terminate the
  registration of its common stock and suspend its Exchange Act reporting obligations,
  effective following the September 18, 2017 merger closing. [SRC: SEC accession 0001577095-17-000201, Form 15-12B]
- Under CIK 0001577095 (ClubCorp Holdings, Inc.), no Form 10-K, 10-Q, or other periodic
  report was filed after the July 2017 10-Q (filed 2017-07-19) and the September 2017
  closing/deregistration filings; a search of EDGAR filing lists for this CIK for
  10-K/10-Q/8-K/15 forms returns nothing dated after September 2017. [SRC: SEC accession 0001577095-17-000201, Form 15-12B; EDGAR filing index for CIK 0001577095]
- Two related historical CIKs on EDGAR under the "ClubCorp" name — ClubCorp Club
  Operations, Inc. (CIK 0001515382) and an earlier ClubCorp entity (CIK 0000929455) —
  also show no Form 10-K filings after 2014 and 2006 respectively, i.e., no filings in
  the 2020-2022 outcome window. [SRC: EDGAR filing index for CIK 0001515382; EDGAR filing index for CIK 0000929455]
- An EDGAR company-name search for "Invited" (the name the business adopted in 2022, see
  below) returns no registered SEC filer entity of that name. [SRC: SEC EDGAR company search, https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&company=invited&type=&dateb=&owner=include&count=100]
- Consequently, no audited public financial statements (net income/loss, impairment,
  segment or club-count disclosure) exist for this business for the ~2020-2022 outcome
  window under any SEC-registered entity identified. This item is coded per the
  no-public-outcome-record rule; the financial/operating trajectory is **UNVERIFIED /
  no public primary-filing record**.

## Realized business record under private ownership (press-sourced, non-financial)
- On April 22, 2022, the company (then operating as ClubCorp) announced it was
  rebranding as "Invited," with the rollout beginning in the following months; the
  company described its portfolio at that time as 161 owned and operated golf and
  country clubs, 205 golf courses, 1,000+ tennis and pickleball courts, 32 city and
  sports clubs, seven stadium clubs, and six BigShots Golf locations, operating across
  27 states, with over 430,000 members and approximately 20,000 peak-season employees. [SRC: https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2022/4/22/2427468/0/en/ClubCorp-Announces-Company-Rebrand-Welcome-To-Invited.html]
- The individual identified as the company's Chief Executive Officer in the April 2022
  rebrand announcement, David Pillsbury, differs from the individual identified as Chief
  Executive Officer (Eric L. Affeldt) in the 2017 closing-era proxy statement; the press
  release does not state the date or circumstances of any CEO transition. [SRC: https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2022/4/22/2427468/0/en/ClubCorp-Announces-Company-Rebrand-Welcome-To-Invited.html]
- The 2022 announcement does not reference the 2017 Apollo acquisition, does not report
  any divestiture, bankruptcy, or dissolution, and reports no financial figures beyond
  employee counts. [SRC: https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2022/4/22/2427468/0/en/ClubCorp-Announces-Company-Rebrand-Welcome-To-Invited.html]

## Items noted but not primary-verifiable
- Reporting has circulated that Apollo Global Management was, around 2022, considering a
  sale or public offering of the rebranded business at a multibillion-dollar valuation;
  this could not be confirmed against a primary source (the source page returned an
  access error on retrieval) and is recorded here as [UNVERIFIED]. [UNVERIFIED]

## Outcome summary (realized record only)
- Because ClubCorp Holdings, Inc. was taken private and deregistered its equity in
  September 2017, and no successor SEC-registered filer for the business (under the
  ClubCorp or "Invited" names) has been identified, there is no public, audited 3-5-year
  outcome record (net income/loss, impairment, segment performance) for this business.
  The only traceable post-closing fact pattern is a 2022 company-sourced rebrand
  announcement describing a portfolio of comparable scale to the pre-merger business
  (roughly 200+ clubs, 430,000+ members) continuing to operate under new ownership, with
  no disclosed divestiture, bankruptcy, or dissolution, and a different named CEO than at
  closing. Per the no-record rule, the financial/operating trajectory itself is coded
  **uncertain (no public primary-filing record)**. [SRC: SEC accession 0001577095-17-000201, Form 15-12B] [SRC: https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2022/4/22/2427468/0/en/ClubCorp-Announces-Company-Rebrand-Welcome-To-Invited.html]

[SLICE END]
